header.userPrompt:
Remove the background-jobs head-of-line bottleneck. Today BackgroundJobsExecutorTask runs ONE
pekko stream over all job types with concurrency 1 (`Sink.foreachAsync(1)`) plus a global
`throttle(100, 1.minute)`, so a slow bank-statement/suggestions job blocks trivial jobs (e.g. emails)
behind it. Change it to N independent per-type streams, each with its own parallelism and timeout,
backed by an ATOMIC claim with a visibility timeout so parallelism is concurrency-safe. Server-only
change; do not touch the web module or the job *handlers'* business logic (only how they're dispatched).

=== 1. Atomic claim with visibility timeout (the core correctness piece) ===
The current `streamPendingJobs` is a plain SELECT with NO locking and NO in-progress state — safe only
because concurrency is 1. Parallelism requires an atomic claim. Add:
  - Schema (Play evolution, Ups only, follow repo evolution conventions, no CHECK constraints). Name the
    new evolution `7.sql` — `6.sql` is reserved by a separate in-flight PR, so skip it to avoid a collision:
      * add a `Running` value to BackgroundJobStatus (enumeratum, Uppercase entry name, like the others).
      * add nullable column `deadline TIMESTAMPTZ` to `background_jobs`. Keep `execute_at` (retry schedule)
        and `error_count` as-is — `execute_at` = when it may run; `deadline` = when a claim expires.
  - A new DAO/repository method `claimJobs(jobType, timeout: Duration, limit: Int)` that atomically claims
    rows in ONE short transaction (commits immediately; processing happens OUTSIDE the tx):
      UPDATE background_jobs SET
        status   = 'RUNNING',
        deadline = ${now} + ${timeout},
        -- count a reclaimed (timed-out/crashed) attempt as an error so a poison job eventually stops:
        error_count = error_count + (CASE WHEN status = 'RUNNING' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
        updated_at = ${now}
      WHERE background_job_id IN (
        SELECT background_job_id FROM background_jobs
        WHERE type = ${jobType}
          AND error_count < ${allowedErrors}
          AND ( (status = 'PENDING' AND execute_at <= ${now})      -- ready
             OR (status = 'RUNNING' AND deadline   <= ${now}) )    -- stuck -> reclaim
        ORDER BY execute_at, background_job_id
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
        LIMIT ${limit}
      )
      RETURNING <all columns>;
    SKIP LOCKED is used ONLY for this brief claim tx (not held across processing); it guarantees two
    concurrent claimers get disjoint rows without blocking. Use the app Clock for ${now} (consistent with
    the rest of the codebase). The CASE-on-old-status increment works because Postgres SET expressions see
    the pre-update row values.
  - Keep setStatusToSuccess / setStatusToFailed as-is (failure still bumps error_count + sets
    execute_at via DelayGenerator backoff and status back to a non-terminal so it retries).

=== 2. Per-type streams in BackgroundJobsExecutorTask ===
Replace the single `streamPendingJobsForever ... throttle(100,1m) ... foreachAsync(1)` with ONE stream
PER BackgroundJobType, started independently and supervised/restarted independently (reuse the existing
`run()` reschedule-on-complete pattern, per stream):
  - Each per-type stream: a source that, on downstream demand, claims ONE job of its type
    (`claimJobs(type, timeout, limit = 1)`); if a job is returned, emit it; if none, wait a short poll
    interval and retry (keep the stream alive forever, like the current unfoldAsync loop). Then
    `.mapAsync(parallelismFor(type))(execute)`. Claiming one-per-demand + mapAsync(parallelism) means at
    most `parallelism` jobs are claimed/in-flight for this process at once (backpressure couples the claim
    rate to free capacity) WITHOUT manual slot bookkeeping — do NOT claim large batches, or jobs sit in
    RUNNING until their deadline falsely lapses.
  - REMOVE the global `throttle(100, 1.minute)` — concurrency is now bounded per type by `parallelism`.
    (External API rate limits, e.g. Bedrock/JEV, are a separate concern handled by keeping those types'
    parallelism low; do NOT add an app-level rate limiter here.)
  - `execute` keeps the existing per-type dispatch match and the success/failure handling; each stream
    only ever receives its own type (the claim filters by type), but `execute` can stay shared.

=== 3. In-process timeout (frees a slot; DB deadline is the cross-crash safety net) ===
Wrap each `execute(job)` in a per-type timeout (e.g. pekko `after` / Future timeout = the type's `timeout`).
On timeout: mark the job failed (setStatusToFailed -> error_count+1 + backoff) and let the stream move on,
so a hung job doesn't occupy a slot forever. The DB `deadline` reclaim in claimJobs covers the case where
the whole process crashed and never marked anything.

=== 4. Per-type config (hardcoded defaults, in config) ===
Add per-type `(parallelism, timeout, pollInterval)` to BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig as a hardcoded default
map keyed by BackgroundJobType (env-overridable is fine but not required). Sensible defaults, rationale =
priority + external limits (tune later):
  - SendEmail:                  parallelism 10, timeout 1m    (SMTP; cheap, high priority)
  - PollReceipt:                parallelism 5,  timeout 1m    (cheap Textract status poll)
  - ProcessDocument:            parallelism 3,  timeout 2m
  - ParseReceipt:               parallelism 3,  timeout 2m
  - ExtractBankStatementDraft:  parallelism 2,  timeout 6m    (expensive; capped by Bedrock)
  - ResolveStatementSuggestions:parallelism 2,  timeout 6m    (JEV per-row; capped externally)
  - PollBankStatement / ParseBankStatement (legacy no-ops): parallelism 1, timeout 30s
A default pollInterval of a few seconds when a type's queue is empty is fine. Every current
BackgroundJobType MUST have an entry (fail loud at startup if one is missing, rather than silently not
processing a type).

=== 5. Idempotency (now structural) ===
This design is at-least-once (a crash past the deadline, or an in-process timeout that actually completed,
re-runs a job). KEEP the existing terminal-status guards (e.g. ProcessDocumentAction skips docs already in
a terminal status). Do NOT introduce any new non-idempotent behavior in the dispatch layer. If any handler
is clearly non-idempotent, call it out in the PR description rather than silently relying on it — do not
change handler business logic in this PR.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===
- Follow docs/guide (antipatterns, backend, data-infra, testing, ci-checklist) and CLAUDE.md.
- Server-only. NO dependency changes (build.sbt/plugins.sbt); revert incidental yarn.lock churn
  (dependencies reviewer). Reuse pekko-streams (already used). No new library.
- Evolutions Ups-only (evolutions reviewer). Prefer enums over strings; Chimney for mapping; never drop a
  Future; stable ORDER BY (execute_at, background_job_id). Fail loud on a missing per-type config.
- Keep DelayGenerator backoff, allowedErrors, BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig.interval, and all existing
  BackgroundJobType/BackgroundJobPayload variants working. Legacy no-op types stay no-ops.
- Attribution: NO Claude session links (claude.ai/ or Claude-Session) in commits or the PR description;
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

=== TESTS (testcontainers Postgres for the claim) ===
- claimJobs: two concurrent claims of the same type return DISJOINT rows (SKIP LOCKED); only PENDING with
  execute_at<=now and error_count<allowedErrors are claimed; a RUNNING row past its deadline IS reclaimed
  and its error_count is incremented; a RUNNING row before its deadline is NOT claimed; filters by type.
- executor: per-type parallelism bound is respected (no more than N of a type in flight); a slow type does
  not block another type (isolation); an in-process timeout marks the job failed and frees the slot; a job
  that exceeds allowedErrors stops being claimed.
- completion/failure still flip status correctly and apply backoff.
- Verify per task with targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; final stage runs the
  full suite.

resultJson.description:
Today `BackgroundJobsExecutorTask` drains every background job type through one pekko stream with `throttle(100, 1.minute)` and `Sink.foreachAsync(1)`. A slow bank-statement extraction or a JEV suggestions job therefore blocks cheap, high-priority work such as SendEmail behind it. The queue read (`BackgroundJobDAO.streamPendingJobs`) is a plain SELECT with no locking and no in-progress state, so it is only correct while concurrency is exactly 1. This epic replaces that with one independent, independently restarted stream per `BackgroundJobType`. Each stream has its own parallelism, timeout and poll interval, and they all sit on an atomic database claim: `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n) RETURNING *`. The claim moves rows to a new `Running` status and gives them a `deadline` (visibility timeout). This makes parallel processing safe across streams and processes, and a job that was claimed but never finished (crash) is reclaimed once its deadline passes, with that attempt counted against `error_count`, so a poison job eventually stops.

Each stream claims one job per unit of downstream demand and runs it through `mapAsyncUnordered(parallelism)`. Backpressure therefore caps the claimed or in-flight jobs per type at `parallelism`, with no manual slot bookkeeping and no batch claims that would leave rows sitting in RUNNING. Each execution is wrapped in an in-process per-type timeout that marks the job failed (the existing `setStatusToFailed` plus `DelayGenerator` backoff) and frees the slot. The DB deadline is the safety net if the whole process crashes. The global throttle is removed and no app-level rate limiter is added: external API limits (Bedrock, JEV) are handled by keeping those types' parallelism low. Handler business logic, the web module and build files stay untouched. `interval`, `allowedErrors` (10), `DelayGenerator` backoff, every existing `BackgroundJobType` and payload, and the legacy no-op types (PollBankStatement, ParseBankStatement) all keep working.

Delivery is at-least-once: a crash past the deadline, or an in-process timeout whose work actually finished, re-runs the job. The existing terminal-status guards stay, and the dispatch layer adds nothing non-idempotent. The PR description must name the handlers that are not idempotent under a re-run rather than fix them here: SendEmail re-sends the email; PollReceiptAction re-enqueues PollReceipt/ParseReceipt follow-up jobs, so duplicates are possible; ProcessDocumentAction can enqueue a duplicate follow-up job if it re-runs before reaching a terminal status; ResolveStatementSuggestions repeats the external JEV calls. Each of these must be checked in code before it goes into the PR description. No Claude session links go in commits or the PR description; `Co-Authored-By: Claude` is allowed. New evolution is `7.sql` because `6.sql` is reserved by another PR.

tasks.title: Atomic job claim with visibility timeout (schema + DAO + repository)
tasks.description:
Add the concurrency-safe claim primitive. Nothing calls it yet, so the current executor keeps working unchanged.

Changes:
- New `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/7.sql`: `-- !Ups` only. `ALTER TABLE background_jobs ADD COLUMN deadline TIMESTAMPTZ NULL;` with a comment explaining that `deadline` is when a RUNNING claim expires and `execute_at` is when the job may run. No DEFAULT, no CHECK, no Downs. Skip 6.sql: it is reserved.
- `BackgroundJobStatus`: add `case object Running`, matching the existing entries.
- `BackgroundJobData`: add `deadline: Option[Instant]` (after `executeAt` is fine). Update `backgroundJobParser` in `repositories/daos/package.scala` to include the "deadline" column in the matching position. `BackgroundJobData.Create` and `BackgroundJobDAO.create` stay as they are, so the column is NULL on insert.
- `BackgroundJobDAO.claimJobs(jobType: BackgroundJobType, timeout: FiniteDuration, limit: Int, allowedErrors: Int = 10)(implicit conn, clock): List[BackgroundJobData]`. This is a single `UPDATE background_jobs SET status=Running, deadline=now+timeout, error_count = error_count + (CASE WHEN status = <Running> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), updated_at=now WHERE background_job_id IN (SELECT background_job_id FROM background_jobs WHERE type = <jobType> AND error_count < allowedErrors AND ((status IN (<Pending>, <Failed>) AND execute_at <= now) OR (status = <Running> AND deadline <= now)) ORDER BY execute_at, background_job_id FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT limit) RETURNING <all columns incl. deadline>`, parsed with `backgroundJobParser.*`.
  - Compute `now = clock.instant()` once in Scala and `deadline = now.plusMillis(timeout.toMillis)`.
  - Bind enum values with `.toString`, as `create`/`setStatus*` already do. Do NOT hardcode 'PENDING' or 'RUNNING' literals (see brief).
  - Include Failed in the ready set: `setStatusToFailed` writes Failed and the current executor retries Failed rows. Leaving it out would stop all retries.
- `BackgroundJobsRepository.claimJobs(jobType, timeout, limit): Future[List[BackgroundJobData]]`, run in `database.withTransaction` on the DatabaseExecutionContext. It is one short tx and commits immediately.
- Leave `streamPendingJobs`, `setStatusToSuccess` and `setStatusToFailed` unchanged.
- `utils/RepositoryUtils.createBackgroundJobData`: add an `executeAt: Instant = Instant.now()` param so tests can seed future jobs without raw SQL.

Tests, in `BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec` under a new `"claimJobs" should { … }` block, against testcontainers Postgres:
- claims a ready Pending job, setting status Running and deadline ≈ now+timeout.
- a Failed job whose execute_at has passed is claimable.
- does not claim a job whose execute_at is in the future, a Success job, or a job with error_count ≥ 10 (reach that by calling `setStatusToFailed(id, Instant.now(), …)` 10 times).
- filters by type.
- respects `limit` and the ORDER BY.
- a Running row before its deadline is not claimed.
- a Running row past its deadline IS reclaimed and its errorCount is incremented by 1. To get there, build a second `BackgroundJobsRepository(repositories.database)(using Executors.databaseEC, Clock.offset(Clock.systemUTC, <timeout + margin>))` and claim with that.
- SKIP LOCKED disjointness, made deterministic: inside `repositories.database.withTransaction { implicit conn => BackgroundJobDAO.claimJobs(...) }`, while that tx is still open, call `repositories.backgroundJobs.claimJobs(...).futureValue`. Assert it returns only the other rows, without blocking. Optionally also fire two concurrent claims and assert the ids are disjoint and complete.

Verify: `sbt "testOnly *BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.description:
Extend `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/config/BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig.scala`.

Changes:
- Add a nested `case class TypeSettings(parallelism: Int, timeout: FiniteDuration, pollInterval: FiniteDuration)`.
- Change the config to `BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig(interval: FiniteDuration, perType: Map[BackgroundJobType, TypeSettings])` and add `def settingsFor(jobType: BackgroundJobType): TypeSettings`.
- Add a hardcoded default map in the companion object. Use a poll interval of a few seconds (e.g. 5.seconds) for every type:
  - SendEmail: parallelism 10, timeout 1.minute
  - PollReceipt: 5, 1.minute
  - ProcessDocument: 3, 2.minutes
  - ParseReceipt: 3, 2.minutes
  - ExtractBankStatementDraft: 2, 6.minutes
  - ResolveStatementSuggestions: 2, 6.minutes
  - PollBankStatement: 1, 30.seconds
  - ParseBankStatement: 1, 30.seconds
  Put a short comment on the rationale: priority plus external limits (Bedrock/JEV), to be tuned later.
- Fail loud at construction. In the case class body (or a validating factory that every path goes through), throw `IllegalStateException` naming the missing types if any `BackgroundJobType.values` has no entry. Also reject parallelism < 1. The Guice `@Provides @Singleton` in `ConfigModule` and the eager `BackgroundJobsExecutorTask` mean this fails app startup.

- the defaults cover every `BackgroundJobType.values`.
- a map missing a type throws at construction, and the message names the type.
- non-positive parallelism is rejected.
- `apply(Configuration("interval" -> "1 minute"))` yields the defaults.

Verify: `sbt "testOnly *BackgroundJobsExecutorConfigSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Per-type job stream runner (claim-on-demand, bounded parallelism, timeout, result recording)
tasks.description:
Add a new, testable component that builds the stream for one job type. It is not wired into the task yet.

Suggested shape, in `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/tasks/BackgroundJobTypeRunner.scala` (the name can be adjusted):
`class BackgroundJobTypeRunner @Inject() (backgroundJobsRepository: BackgroundJobsRepository)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext, actorSystem: ActorSystem, clock: Clock)` with
`def source(jobType: BackgroundJobType, settings: BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig.TypeSettings, dispatch: BackgroundJobData => Future[Unit]): Source[Unit, NotUsed]`.

Behaviour:
1. Claim source: `Source.unfoldAsync(())(_ => claimNext().map(job => Some(((), job))))`. `claimNext()` calls `backgroundJobsRepository.claimJobs(jobType, visibility, limit = 1)`. If it returns a job, emit it. If it returns Nil, `org.apache.pekko.pattern.after(settings.pollInterval)(claimNext())`. This loops forever and claims only when pulled.
2. Run `.mapAsyncUnordered(settings.parallelism)(runOne)`. It must be Unordered: ordered `mapAsync` would let one slow job hold completed slots, which is head-of-line blocking again inside a type. Do not add `.async`, `.buffer` or batch claims, because extra buffering pre-claims jobs that then sit in RUNNING.
3. `runOne(job)`:
   - Race `dispatch(job)` against `after(settings.timeout)(Future.failed(new TimeoutException(...)))` using `Future.firstCompletedOf`. Guard a synchronous throw from `dispatch` with `Future.delegate` or an equivalent.
   - On success, call `setStatusToSuccess(job.id)`.
   - On any NonFatal failure, including the timeout, keep the existing logic: `executeAt = clock.instant().plus(DelayGenerator.createDelay(job.errorCount), ChronoUnit.MINUTES)`, `logger.warn(...)`, then `setStatusToFailed(job.id, executeAt, ex.getMessage)`.
   - Never drop a Future. When the timeout wins, attach an `onComplete` to the original dispatch future that logs its late outcome, but do not record it.
4. Claim visibility: pass the type timeout plus a small named margin constant (e.g. 30.seconds, with a comment), so the in-process timeout always fires and records before the DB deadline lapses. The DB deadline is only the crash safety net.

Move the success/failure recording out of `BackgroundJobsExecutorTask.execute` into this runner, so the task in the next task only supplies `dispatch`. For now the task keeps its own copy; it is replaced in the next task.

Tests: new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/tasks/BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec.scala`. Extend `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils with BeforeAndAfterAll`, with its own ActorSystem as in BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec.
- Build the runner over `repositories.backgroundJobs` with fake `dispatch` functions.
- Use small settings (e.g. pollInterval 50.millis) and materialize with `.viaMat(KillSwitches.single)(Keep.right).toMat(Sink.ignore)(Keep.both).run()`. Shut the kill switch down at the end of each test.
- Gate completion with test-controlled Promises, not sleeps. Use `eventually` with a patience config for assertions.

Cases:
- Parallelism bound: seed more than N jobs of one type. A dispatch that increments an AtomicInteger and blocks on a Promise must observe max in-flight == N, never more. After releasing, all jobs are Success.
- Isolation: one type's stream has its jobs blocked forever while another type's stream completes all its jobs.
- Timeout: a dispatch that never completes, with a short timeout. The job ends up Failed with errorCount 1, execute_at moved forward, and status_details mentioning the timeout. The slot frees, so a subsequent job of that type still runs.
- Failure: dispatch fails, giving status Failed, errorCount+1 and execute_at ≈ now + 2^errorCount minutes.
- Success flips status to Success.
- allowedErrors cut-off: give the runner `Clock.systemUTC` but give the repository a `Clock.offset(+2 days)`. Backoff then never defers reclaim, so an always-failing job is dispatched exactly 10 times and then no longer claimed.

Read job state back through `claimJobs` on another repo clock, or a small read via the DAO parser inside the test. Raw SQL reads are already used in other specs, but seed only via `RepositoryUtils`.

Verify: `sbt "testOnly *BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Wire per-type streams into BackgroundJobsExecutorTask and remove the global stream
tasks.description:
Switch the executor to N independent per-type streams and delete the code this orphans.

Changes:
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/tasks/BackgroundJobsExecutorTask.scala`:
  - Inject `BackgroundJobTypeRunner` instead of `StreamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction`.
  - Keep `execute` as the per-type dispatch match only. That is the existing `job.type match` with the payload `asOpt` checks and the legacy no-op branch for PollBankStatement/ParseBankStatement, and `sendEmail` stays. Rename it to `dispatch` if that is clearer. The success/failure recording now lives in the runner, so remove it here.
  - For each `BackgroundJobType.values`, call `config.settingsFor(t)` at construction time; this fails loud if one is missing. Then schedule a per-type `run(t)` with `actorSystem.scheduler.scheduleOnce(config.interval)`.
  - `run(t)` = `runner.source(t, settings, dispatch).runWith(Sink.ignore)`. Its `onComplete` reschedules only that type after `config.interval`: `logger.error` on Failure, quiet reschedule on Success, the same pattern as today but per stream.
  - Remove `throttle(100, 1.minute)` and `Sink.foreachAsync(1)` and the comment about them. Clean up unused imports (`DurationInt` etc.); `-Werror` fails on them.
- Delete `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/internal/StreamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction.scala`, `BackgroundJobsRepository.streamPendingJobs` and `BackgroundJobDAO.streamPendingJobs`, plus any imports they leave unused, e.g. `PekkoStream` / `anorm.postgresql.*` if they become unused.
- Migrate the test callers of `streamPendingJobs`:
  - `BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec`: drop the `streamPendingJobs` block, since claimJobs coverage replaces it. Rewrite the `setStatusToFailed` and `setStatusToSuccess` "work" cases to assert via `claimJobs`. After failure with executeAt=now, the job is claimable with errorCount 1 and statusDetails set. After success, nothing is claimable.
  - `UsersRepositorySpec`, at lines ~162, ~192 and ~226: replace the job-count checks with `repositories.backgroundJobs.claimJobs(BackgroundJobType.SendEmail, 1.minute, 10).futureValue.length must be(1)`. Remove the now-unused `Sink` and ActorSystem imports if any.
- Update `docs/guide/backend.md` § Background jobs:
  - statuses are now pending/running/success/failed, plus the `deadline` column.
  - replace the paragraph about throttle and `foreachAsync(1)` with the per-type streams description: atomic SKIP LOCKED claim, `parallelism` / `timeout` / `pollInterval` from `BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig`, and at-least-once delivery, so handlers must be idempotent.
  - in "Adding a new job type", add a step saying to add a `TypeSettings` entry, and note that startup fails without one.
- Do not touch handler actions, `web/`, `build.sbt` or `project/`. If `yarn.lock` shows churn, revert it.

Verify:
- `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
- `sbt "testOnly *BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec *UsersRepositorySpec *BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec *BackgroundJobsExecutorConfigSpec"`
- one controller spec that runs the live executor, e.g. `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec"`, to confirm the app still boots with the eager executor.

The full suite runs in the final stage.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES / DIRS
- server/ = the Play backend, which is the only module touched. Layers: controllers → actions → repositories (Anorm DAOs). Background jobs live in the `background_jobs` table (2.sql). Columns: background_job_id UUID PK, type TEXT, payload JSONB, status TEXT, status_details TEXT NULL, error_count INT DEFAULT 0, execute_at, created_at, updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ). There is an index on execute_at.
- Evolutions: server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/{1..5}.sql exist. The new one MUST be 7.sql because 6.sql is reserved by another PR. Ups only (`-- !Ups`), no Downs, no CHECK constraints, no DEFAULT clauses (RULE-DB-016), TIMESTAMPTZ, one evolution file per PR.

KEY FILES
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/tasks/BackgroundJobsExecutorTask.scala
  - Eager singleton, bound in modules/TasksModule.scala.
  - Constructor injects config, StreamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction, EmailApi, BackgroundJobsRepository and the handler actions: ProcessDocumentAction, PollReceiptAction, ParseReceiptAction (actions/documents), ExtractBankStatementDraftAction and ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction (actions/bankstatements).
  - Implicits: (ec: ExecutionContext, actorSystem: ActorSystem, clock: Clock).
  - `execute(job)` matches on job.`type` and does `job.payload.asOpt[BackgroundJobPayload.X]`, returning Future.failed(RuntimeException) on a bad payload.
  - PollBankStatement | ParseBankStatement are legacy no-ops (Future.unit + log).
  - On result it calls `backgroundJobsRepository.setStatusToSuccess(job.id)`, or recoverWith NonFatal → `executeAt = clock.instant().plus(DelayGenerator.createDelay(job.errorCount), ChronoUnit.MINUTES)`, then `logger.warn`, then `setStatusToFailed(job.id, executeAt, ex.getMessage)`.
  - `run()`: `streamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction().throttle(100,1.minute).runWith(Sink.foreachAsync(1)(execute))`, then onComplete reschedules `run()` after config.interval (logger.error on Failure).
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/internal/StreamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction.scala: unfoldAsync loop re-running repository.streamPendingJobs every 10s. Its only main-code caller is the task.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BackgroundJobsRepository.scala
  - `class BackgroundJobsRepository @Inject()(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`.
  - Methods: create, streamPendingJobs (autocommit=false streaming connection), setStatusToFailed(id, executeAt: Instant, failReason): Future[Unit], setStatusToSuccess(id): Future[Unit].
  - Each method is a `Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => DAO... } }`. Writes should use withTransaction (RULE-DB-001).
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BackgroundJobDAO.scala: `object BackgroundJobDAO` using `import anorm.*` and SQL"""...""" interpolation.
  - streamPendingJobs(allowedErrors: Int = 10, ...)(implicit conn, clock) selects `status != Success AND execute_at <= now AND error_count < allowedErrors ORDER BY execute_at, background_job_id`. Note that FAILED rows ARE retried today.
  - setStatusToFailed sets status=Failed, status_details, error_count+1, execute_at; it throws RuntimeException if 0 rows are affected.
  - setStatusToSuccess sets status=Success.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/package.scala: `backgroundJobParser = Macro.parser[BackgroundJobData]("background_job_id","type","payload","status","status_details","error_count","execute_at","created_at","updated_at")`. The column list must match the case class field order. It also has `backgroundJobStatusColumn` / `backgroundJobTypeColumn` via enumColumn(withNameInsensitiveOption).
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/models/BackgroundJobData.scala: case class (id, `type`, payload: JsValue, status, statusDetails: Option[String], errorCount: Int, executeAt, createdAt, updatedAt), plus `Create` (id, type, payload: BackgroundJobPayload, status, executeAt, createdAt, updatedAt).
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/models/jobs/BackgroundJobStatus.scala (Success, Pending, Failed) and BackgroundJobType.scala (SendEmail, ProcessDocument, PollBankStatement, ParseBankStatement, PollReceipt, ParseReceipt, ExtractBankStatementDraft, ResolveStatementSuggestions). Both are enumeratum `sealed trait X extends EnumEntry with Uppercase`, `val values = findValues`. BackgroundJobPayload.scala has the payload case classes.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/config/BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig.scala: `case class BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig(interval: FiniteDuration)` with a custom toString, plus `apply(config: Configuration)` reading "interval". It is provided in modules/ConfigModule.scala (`@Provides @Singleton`, reads `backgroundJobsExecutorTask` from application.conf: interval = 1 minutes, env NOTIFICATIONS_TASK_INTERVAL).
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/util/DelayGenerator.scala: `createDelay(retry: Int, factor: Int = 2): Long` = factor^retry (minutes as used).
- docs/guide/backend.md §"Background jobs" (~lines 266-310) describes the old throttle/foreachAsync(1) design; update it when the wiring changes.

CRITICAL GOTCHA — enum string representation
- The DB stores `status.toString` / `type.toString`, i.e. the case-object name such as "Pending", "Running", "SendEmail". It does NOT store entryName (Uppercase). Parsing is case-insensitive. Controller specs compare with `UPPER(type) = entryName`.
- In claimJobs SQL, bind `${BackgroundJobStatus.Running.toString}` etc., exactly as create/setStatus* do. Never write literal 'PENDING' or 'RUNNING' in SQL, because they would never match.
- The ready set must be `status IN (Pending, Failed)`, because setStatusToFailed leaves rows in Failed and they must keep retrying.
- Postgres SET expressions see pre-update values, so `error_count + CASE WHEN status = Running THEN 1 ELSE 0 END` works on the old status.
- Postgres 13 (testcontainers) supports `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` in a subquery of UPDATE ... RETURNING. Parse with `.as(backgroundJobParser.*)`.
- Compute now/deadline in Scala from the injected Clock: `clock.instant()`, `now.plusMillis(timeout.toMillis)`. Pre-existing DAO lines using Instant.now() are not yours to change.

PEKKO NOTES (pekko 1.6.0, pekko-stream already a dependency; no new libs)
- Claim-on-demand: `Source.unfoldAsync` emits only when pulled, which pairs with `.mapAsyncUnordered(parallelism)` to cap claimed or in-flight jobs at parallelism.
- Use Unordered. Ordered mapAsync holds slots behind a slow head element.
- Keep the graph fused: no `.async` or `.buffer`.
- Timeout: `org.apache.pekko.pattern.after(d)(Future.failed(new java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException(..)))` raced with `Future.firstCompletedOf`. Log the losing dispatch future's late outcome; never drop a Future.
- Tests can stop forever-streams with `KillSwitches.single`.

TESTING CONVENTIONS (docs/guide/testing.md)
- ScalaTest AnyWordSpec, `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*`, `.futureValue`.
- `"method" should { "behaviour" in ... }`: never repeat the class name in the subject.
- DB tests extend `net.wiringbits.core.RepositorySpec` (PostgresSpec: a fresh postgres:13 container per test, evolutions applied). Use `withRepositories(clock = ...) { implicit repositories => ... }`, which gives a RepositoryComponents with `.database` and `.backgroundJobs`; patience is 30s.
- Seed via `utils/RepositoryUtils` (`createBackgroundJobData(id, backgroundJobType, status, payload)`), never raw INSERTs. Raw SELECTs for assertions already exist in BankStatementRepositorySpec and the controller specs.
- To get a different clock for one repository: `new BackgroundJobsRepository(repositories.database)(using utils.Executors.databaseEC, Clock.offset(Clock.systemUTC, java.time.Duration.ofMinutes(n)))`.
- The test DatabaseExecutionContext delegates to the global EC, and the Hikari pool has more than one connection, so a nested claim while a withTransaction is open works.
- BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec creates its own `ActorSystem` and terminates it in afterAll; copy that for stream tests.
- Callers of `streamPendingJobs` today: BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec and UsersRepositorySpec (3 "produce a notification" tests at lines ~162/192/226).
- Controller specs (PlayPostgresSpec / GuiceOneServerPerTest) boot the real app, so the live executor runs. Some tests schedule jobs 365 days ahead to keep the executor away from them.
- Mockito is only for controller specs.

BUILD / WORKFLOW
- Typecheck with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (`-Werror`: unused imports and deprecations fail).
- Targeted tests: `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`. Do not run the full `sbt test` inside a task.
- Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.
- No build.sbt, plugins.sbt or web/ changes; revert any yarn.lock churn.
- Prefer enums over strings, Chimney for multi-field case-class mapping, and `logger.warn` for recoverable job failures / `logger.error` for unexpected ones.
- Fail loud: throw at startup on a missing per-type config, no silent defaults.
- Do not change handler business logic. ProcessDocumentAction, PollReceiptAction and ParseReceiptAction keep their terminal-status skip guards, and ExtractBankStatementDraftAction skips drafts that are not in Processing.
